quotes.text: The truth, Power Automate is brilliant for personal productivity, but allergic to industrial scale processing. Throw ten thousand records at it and it panics.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sharp framing of where Power Automate stops scaling.

quotes.text: The lesson is simple. Simplicity doesn't equal scalability, Drag and drop logic doesn't substitute for throughput engineering.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concise principle against treating low-code flows as infrastructure.

quotes.text: The mature approach isn't exile. It's division of labor. Use power Automate for human interaction points and logic apps for the actual heavy lifting.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear recommendation for a hybrid architecture.

quotes.text: Power Automate isn't broken, it's just being abused. It was designed for prototypes and personal productivity, the quick wins that save minutes, not the architectures meant to sustain enterprises.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Balanced verdict on the tool's intended purpose.

quotes.text: Real professionals know the difference between convenience and competence. Power Automate gives you simplicity. Logic apps gives you control when scale matters.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable summary of the platform trade-off.

chapters.title: Power Automate is not an integration engine
Two invisible failure points: throttling and licensing
Enter Logic Apps: the professional alternative

takeaways: Power Automate was built for citizen developers and personal productivity, not mission-critical integration at enterprise scale.
Throttling and licensing are the two invisible failure points: connector limits silently stop flows, and per-user, per-flow and premium connector costs multiply as flows spread.
Use a hybrid pattern where Power Automate handles human interaction and hands heavy processing to Azure Logic Apps with Application Insights monitoring and managed identities.
hook: Power Automate flows that work for one team often fail silently or get expensive once they carry enterprise workloads. This episode is for makers, architects and IT pros running mission-critical automation. You learn when to move workflows to Azure Logic Apps and how a hybrid pattern keeps user convenience while gaining scale and control.
